personal_allowance_2024_2026.notes: Frozen at £12,570; Finance Act 2026 s.10 extends the freeze to 2030-31

basic_rate_limit_2024_2026.notes: Basic rate band £37,700 (limit £50,270 with the personal allowance), frozen to 2030-31 per Finance Act 2026 s.10

ni_employee_rate_2024.notes: Reduced from 12% to 8% on 6 Jan 2024 (Spring Budget)

pension_annual_allowance_2024_2026.notes: Raised to £60,000 from April 2023, unchanged since

ssp_weekly_rate_2024_2025.notes: £116.75/week for 2024/25 only (2025/26 is £118.75, see ssp_weekly_rate_2025_2026); paid by employer for up to 28 weeks; self-employed not eligible

ni_lower_earnings_limit_2024.notes: £123/week in 2024/25; must earn at least this to qualify for SSP

income_protection_coverage_range.notes: ABI guidance: 50–70% of gross salary; no fixed premium benchmark as premiums vary by age, health, and occupation

life_insurance_salary_multiple.notes: 10× annual gross salary is the widely cited MoneyHelper / ABI rule of thumb; actual need depends on mortgage and dependants

employer_liability_minimum_cover.notes: Minimum £5 million cover required under Employers' Liability (Compulsory Insurance) Act 1969; most policies provide £10 million

ssp_weekly_rate_2026_2027.notes: £123.25/week or 80% of average weekly earnings if lower; from 6 April 2026 SSP has no Lower Earnings Limit test and no waiting days (repo previously had £116.75)

employer_ni_2025_onward.notes: NICs (Secondary Class 1 Contributions) Act 2025 s.1: employer rate 15% from 6 April 2025, no end date, so enacted for 2027/28. Secondary threshold £5,000/year for 2025/26 and 2026/27 (gov.uk employer rates pages); repo previously had 13.8% above £9,100 for 2025 and 2026. 2024/25 stays 13.8% above £9,100

employer_ni_secondary_threshold_2027_28.notes: £5,000/year (£96/week) announced for 2027/28; the 2025 Act specifies it only for 2025/26. Repo carries the 2026/27 value (£5,000)

income_tax_2027_28_enacted.notes: Finance Act 2026 (Royal Assent 18 Mar 2026): s.10 personal allowance £12,570 and basic rate band £37,700 for 2027-28 to 2030-31; s.4 dividend ordinary/upper rates 10.75%/35.75%; s.9 savings starting rate limit £5,000. Dividend allowance £500 (ITA 2007 s.13A)

savings_property_rates_2027_28.notes: Finance Act 2026 s.5 (savings) and s.7 (property) enact 22%/42%/47% for 2027/28, which the repo uses. Budget 2026 announces 24%/44%/49% from 2027/28 via Finance Bill 2026-27, not yet enacted: announced, unconfirmed; switch only after Royal Assent

cgt_isa_pension_2027_28.notes: CGT 18%/24% (TCGA 1992 s.1H), annual exempt amount £3,000 (s.1K), BADR rate 18% (s.169N); ISA £20,000 (ISA Regs 1998 reg 4ZA); pension annual allowance £60,000 (FA 2004 s.228), taper trigger £260,000 / minimum £10,000 (s.228ZA)

announced_not_legislated_2027_28.notes: Budget 2026 figures for 2027/28 that do NOT drive calculations (repo carries 2026/27 values, results flagged Likely with a warning): higher/additional rate limit £125,140, rates 20/40/45%, taper threshold £100,000, marriage allowance £1,260, NI primary threshold £12,570 / UEL £50,270 / rates 8% and 2% / Class 4 6% and 2%, personal savings allowance £1,000/£500, dividend additional rate 39.35%, trading allowance rising to £3,000 from 6 Apr 2027, BADR lifetime limit falling from £1,000,000 to £500,000 from 6 Apr 2027, LEL £133/week, Employment Allowance £10,500, MPAA £10,000, Junior ISA £9,000

ssp_weekly_rate_2027_28.notes: £127.55/week proposed for 2027/28 (published 11 Nov 2026, titled 'Proposed'); repo carries £123.25 and income protection guidance is flagged Likely with a warning

student_loan_thresholds_2027_28.notes: Not modelled in repo. Announced for 2027/28: Plan 1 £28,005; Plan 2 £29,385 (frozen); Plan 5 £26,025; Postgraduate £21,000; Plan 4 and rates not published

scottish_bands_2026_27.notes: Discrepancy, repo NOT changed: the repo 2026 bands are a projection of 2025/26 (starter to £2,827, basic to £14,921 taxable income). gov.scot lists 2026/27 bands (starter £12,571-£16,537, basic £16,538-£29,526; intermediate to £43,662, higher to £75,000, advanced to £125,140), which would be taxable-income uppers of about £3,967 and £16,956 for the first two bands, but labels them 'proposed' and passage of the Scottish Rate Resolution is unverified. Update only once confirmed

scottish_bands_2027_28.notes: No 2027/28 Scottish bands published; repo carries the 2026 projection forward and the 2027 result is flagged Likely
